rubric_notes: Materially wrong relationship-bearing classification: places archaeal histones (HMfB) inside family a.22.1.1 with the eukaryotic core histones and calls them 'same family', whereas SCOPe 2.08 puts them in a separate family a.22.1.2 (hard ceiling bio <= 2). Omits the bacterial histone-fold family a.22.1.4 and the release. Lists Dpb3/4, POLE3/4, CHRAC, CENP-S/X/T/W as superfamily members without SCOPe support. Superfamily/fold placement, homology-versus-function limits and non-relationship of H1/HU/IHF are handled well, but no evidence bundle and family numbering admitted to be from memory. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct central inference (superfamily a.204.1 remote homology, different families, no function transfer) with good limits. But omits the family sccs a.204.1.2 / a.204.1.4, mislabels fold and superfamily as 'MazG-like' instead of 'all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatases', admits unverified recall, and presents a conserved acidic metal-binding active site as a SCOPe-supported statement without evidence. No release-specific support. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Reasoning is complete and careful: superfamily c.55.1 as remote homology, conserved two-lobe RNase H-like core with nucleotide cleft, and explicit rejection of substrate, EC number, regulation, oligomerization, cellular role, active-site residue and template transfer; fold-level similarity correctly distinguished from homology. But the answer admits it is unsure of and omits the family sccs identifiers c.55.1.1, c.55.1.3, c.55.1.4 required by must_include, and supplies no API evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Biological interpretation is sound: divergent remote homology in one superfamily, fold-only similarity insufficient, explicit rejection of function/metal/assembly transfer, convergence of haem catalase and Mn-SOD correctly separated, and required evidence (ligand set, metal preference, second shell, oligomeric state, assays) listed. Factual support is weak: no release, no SUNIDs, family codes given only 'roughly' from memory, and rubrerythrin/bacterioferritin/MMO/desaturase are described as separate 'related families' when they are proteins within a.25.1.1 and a.25.1.2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Biological inference is complete: superfamily b.6.1 implies probable common ancestor, function is family-specific, copper/electron transfer rejected with specific required evidence (conserved ligands, metal in structure, spectroscopy, redox, mutagenesis); no must_avoid violation. However, it is memory-based with no evidence bundle, gives no release, and omits the required family identifiers b.6.1.1, b.6.1.5, b.6.1.6 (explicitly unsure of family sccs). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Strong biology: superfamily d.15.1 = probable common ancestry on beta-grasp core, mechanistic contrast of conjugation vs p97 N-domain binding vs Ras-GTP binding, explicit rejection of UBX->Ras, RBD->p97, conjugation and interface transfers, requires family-level/experimental evidence. Factual support weak: no evidence bundle, no release cited, and the family SCCS codes (d.15.1.1/.2/.5) and sunids are never given (self-flagged as from memory).

Correctly places the three domains as separate families in superfamily c.23.1 (fold c.23), interprets this as remote homology rather than family-level relatedness, distinguishes fold from superfamily, and explicitly rejects transfer of Asp phosphorylation/phosphotransfer, decarboxylase catalysis, KaiA clock function, FliM binding and templates; domain recruitment into larger proteins is addressed. Gives c.23.1.1 but admits it did not verify the ODC (c.23.1.4) and KaiA (c.23.1.5) family sccs, so two of the three required family identifiers are missing; no evidence bundle. Peripheral imprecision: places ODC catalysis in a 'PLP-binding barrel domain' (the Lactobacillus ODC whose wing is c.23.1.4 has a c.67.1.5 fold-type I major domain, not a barrel). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Central inference is right: separate superfamily inside the barrel-sandwich-hybrid fold means fold-level similarity only, no homology asserted across superfamilies, convergence or remote divergence possible, no function transfer. However it never names b.84.5, b.84.5.1 or any release/sunid, does not address the family level explicitly, and asserts 'no detectable sequence relationship' as fact without support. Admits it is recalled knowledge. Must_include 1 and 3 not met. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Overall conclusion (same fold, separate superfamilies, no homology from fold) is right, but the superfamily identifiers are swapped: fumarate reductase subunits are given as f.21.1, nitrate reductase gamma as f.21.2, di-heme cytochromes as f.21.3 (actual: f.21.1 di-heme, f.21.2 fumarate reductase, f.21.3 nitrate reductase). Wrong superfamily assignment triggers the bio<=2 ceiling. Also asserts as fact that the groups have no detectable sequence similarity and differ in heme geometry and helix packing without any evidence, leaning toward a positive non-homology claim. No sunids, release, or bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Central conclusion correct: remote homology with divergent function, no transfer of enzymatic function, cofactor, catalytic residues or regulatory behaviour; good domain vs whole-protein discussion (GroES-like catalytic domain not part of the relationship). However it states 'a same-fold or same-superfamily relationship is therefore evidence for distant ancestry', blurring the fold/superfamily distinction that SCOP reserves for homology, so one important distinction is muddied (not asserted as proof, so no hard ceiling). No bundle; only c.2.1.1 given (hedged), c.2.1.8 and c.2.1.9 omitted. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

No lookup; admits it rests on general knowledge. Does not state the shared family k.40.1.1, sunid 100905, or the 'not a true family' comment, and suggests 'if they do not share a superfamily' as if unknown. Asserts similarity 'reflects convergent engineering, not descent' without evidence. Correct small element is that both sit in the Designed proteins class. Bio 1, factual 1.

Correct direction (own fold/superfamily in 1.69 to shared c.23.14 superfamily with separate families) and sound limits on function transfer, clearly flagged as unverified memory. No evidence, no SIDs, no family sccs, no 1.69 c.137.1.1 placement; factual support sparse. No must_avoid violations.

Answered from memory with explicit 'under that reading' hedge. Correctly puts d1a14h2 in class l Artifacts and d1a14h1 in Ig fold/superfamily V-set, class b, but omits SCCS l.1.1.1, the Tags lineage, N-terminal Tags/Synthetic, and any identifiers. Homology reasoning is correct (engineered sequence, not ancestry; rely on d1a14h1) and includes a reasonable alternative caveat, but support is sparse and unverified.

Pretrained-only refusal with an empty bundle: no specific sids, boundaries, classifications, or release change for 1acc. General domains-as-modules and homology-search reasoning is sound but ungrounded in the actual case. Does not fabricate, which is appropriate, but fails the specific factual requirements.

From memory, no SIDs, boundaries or sccs. Includes a Jab1/MPN domain in the five-domain set and omits the bromodomain; attributes 3jb9 to S. cerevisiae (SCOPe lists S. pombe); calls the N-terminal domain helical (it is class d a+b). Mosaic concept and no-function-transfer limits are sound, but wrong domain composition caps reasoning at 2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Generic repeat-protein explanation with no release evidence, no protein/species identities, no lineage names, and no 're' annotation or representative repeat unit. Explicitly declines to give entry-specific facts. Limits on specificity transfer are reasonable.

No endpoint access; states stable 2.08 from recollection (correct) and the periodic label form '2.08-YYYY-MM-DD' but no actual periodic identifier, so the first must_include is only partially met. Semantics are correct: cite stable release as primary, cite exact periodic label as a required second identifier when periodic-only entries are used, do not treat periodic as the stable reference, periodic adds newly released PDB entries. No fabrication. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. No evidence retrieved; no SIDs, sunids or explicit family given, and fold a.47 is misnamed 'spectrin-repeat-like' (STAT-like). Opening sentence is muddled but the body correctly argues fragments should not define a fold, the full domain is the reference, and function should not transfer. The SCOPe fragment comment and 'ms' flag are absent, so the fragment-driven spectrin resemblance and its resolution are not addressed. Avoids claiming unrelatedness.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Clear divergence-within-c.2.1 versus convergence-across-folds framing, with independent reasons (topology, strand order, binding geometry) rather than superfamily placement alone, and a caveat that undetected remote relationships remain possible. Evidence integration (sequence/HMM, topology, core, function) and classification-level semantics are correct; explicit transfer limits. Factual: identifiers and family examples (c.2.1 families, c.3, FNR-like, DHS-like, AKR TIM barrel, ICDH fold) are correct but from memory with no release-scoped retrieval, flagged by the answer.

Correct direction and inference (2.04 separate superfamilies/folds to 2.08 shared b.18.1 superfamily, different families, structure-discovered remote homology) with good caveats and no must_avoid violation. But from memory with empty bundle: does not name the 2.04 ColG superfamily b.23.2 and omits family numbers b.18.1.36/b.18.1.3, flagging them unverified. Supporting identifiers sparse and imprecise.

Keeps family-level homology and gives generic template/benchmark hygiene advice, but reads hf as a 'heterogeneous or non-standard entry' marker and states 'family membership justifies the shared homeodomain fold', missing the heterogeneous-fold meaning and violating the must_avoid on assuming geometry from family placement. No release, identifiers, boundaries, comments, or evidence; admits it could not confirm the entries' contexts. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Good fragment-aware reasoning: classification unchanged, coverage checks, normalise by aligned residues, complete domain as representative, fragment secondary and flagged, diversity on core-covered region, no function transfer. But no API evidence: no release, boundaries, sunids, or the actual fr definition (described loosely as 'incomplete or only a partial piece of the construct'). Admits it could not check boundaries. Lineage correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Correct recommendation; family = close ancestry, new family in existing superfamily asserts homology to that superfamily; superfamily = probable common origin from structure plus functional/sequence evidence, left open rather than asserting independent origin; new fold requires genuine topology difference; revisable hypothesis; rejects function/active-site transfer. Backbone-only template remark is appropriately limited. No fabricated facts, honestly states no release checked. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Reasoning is complete: superfamily placement as probable common ancestry, shared two-lobe ATP phosphotransfer scaffold with lineage-specific substrate surfaces, explicit refusal to transfer substrate class, ePK activation-loop regulation, PI3K subunit regulation, inhibitor sensitivity or templates, PIKK caveat, and a six-point evidence list (family-level HMM alignment, structural comparison in matched states, biochemistry, cellular/genetic data, regulatory-interface mutagenesis, resistance assays). Factual support is weak: no evidence bundle, d.144/d.144.1 given from recall, and the required family identifiers d.144.1.7/d.144.1.6/d.144.1.4 are omitted as unverifiable. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
